what_its_for: Zolmitriptan is used to treat migraine headaches with or without aura in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is NOT used to prevent migraines or treat other types of headaches.
how_to_take: Take zolmitriptan as soon as your migraine headache begins. You can take it with or without food. If you are using the regular tablet, swallow it whole with water. If you are using the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew or swallow it whole. If you are using the nasal spray, blow your nose gently first, then spray one dose into one nostril. Do not use more than your prescribed dose in one day.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 2.5 mg for tablets or orally disintegrating tablets, or 2.5 mg to 5 mg for the nasal spray. If your migraine comes back after the first dose, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than 10 mg in any 24-hour period. Always use the lowest dose that works for you.
missed_dose: Zolmitriptan is taken only when you have a migraine — it is not taken on a regular daily schedule. There is no missed dose to worry about. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store zolmitriptan tablets and orally disintegrating tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medication out of reach of children. Store the nasal spray at room temperature and keep it in its original packaging until use.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking zolmitriptan within 24 hours of using another triptan medication (such as sumatriptan or rizatriptan) or an ergotamine-type medicine. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol, as it can worsen headaches and increase side effects. Do not use more than 10 headache treatment days per month to avoid medication overuse headache (rebound headaches).
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; shortness of breath; sudden severe headache different from your usual migraine; weakness or numbness on one side of the body; slurred speech; vision changes; fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe stomach pain; or if your headaches are getting worse or happening more often. Also contact your doctor if the medicine stops working for you.
when_it_works: Zolmitriptan usually begins to relieve migraine pain within 1 to 2 hours after taking it. Most people feel significant relief within 2 hours. The nasal spray may work a little faster for some people. If you have no relief after the first dose, do not take a second dose without checking with your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using zolmitriptan if you are pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medication in these situations is not fully established. Older adults (65+): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Children: Zolmitriptan is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or advise against using this medication if you have significant liver or kidney disease. Heart conditions: Do not use this medication if you have a history of heart disease, stroke, or uncontrolled high blood pressure without first speaking to your doctor.
